PCB Circuit Board Coasters vs GABNICO Stone Coasters: Tech Geek or Minimalist?

Real circuit board coasters with gold immersion finish for $16.99, or diatomaceous earth stone coasters for ~$13.99? One is a conversation piece for your desk, the other is an absorbent workhorse. We put them head-to-head across six categories to help you choose.

Published September 2026 · Based on verified Amazon product data

Coasters are one of those things you don't think about until you set a sweating glass down on an unprotected surface. Then suddenly, you care a lot. The good news is you have options — and they don't all look the same.

The PCB Circuit Board Coasters are exactly what they sound like: real decommissioned circuit boards, cut and finished into drink coasters with an immersion gold surface. They're thin, rigid, industrial-chic, and an absolute magnet for conversation at your desk. The GABNICO Diatomaceous Earth Stone Coasters take the opposite approach: thick absorbent stone that wicks moisture away from your glass and dries instantly. Two completely different philosophies, both under $17.

We tested both for style, function, durability, and value to help you figure out which set belongs on your coffee table.

🏆 PCB Circuit Board Coasters Our Pick

$16.99

These aren't printed replicas — they're real circuit boards salvaged and finished into drink coasters. Each coaster has actual conductive traces, solder pads, and component footprints, preserved under an ultra-thin immersion gold layer for a unique industrial aesthetic. GABNICO Home Stone Coaster Set of 6 — The Absorbent Minimalist

$13.99

GABNICO's stone coasters are made from diatomaceous earth — a naturally porous sedimentary rock that's been a darling of the coaster world for good reason. These coasters are 3.93 inches in diameter, significantly larger than the PCB coasters, and about 1/4 inch thick. The dark grey color gives them a clean, modern look that blends into most desk and table settings.

The science is simple: diatomaceous earth is packed with microscopic pores that suck moisture out of condensation almost instantly. Set a cold drink down, and within 10-15 seconds, the coaster surface is dry again. The absorbed moisture evaporates naturally from the stone's underside, so the coaster self-regenerates. No puddles, no rings, no soggy cardboard coaster replacement cycle.

These are the coasters you buy when you want something that works invisibly and well. They don't scream for attention on your coffee table — and for a lot of people, that's exactly the point. They come as a set of 6 with a bamboo holder included, making them easy to store and display.

Style and Aesthetic: Night and Day

This is the defining difference between the two. The PCB coasters are maximalist, industrial, and attention-grabbing — genuine circuit boards with visible traces in gold and green, an almost jewelry-like finish that celebrates circuit board design as functional art. They're not subtle, and they shouldn't be.

The GABNICO stone coasters are the opposite: invisible by design. Dark grey with a matte texture, they quietly sit under your glass and do their job unnoticed. If your aesthetic is minimalist or modern, these blend right in.

Our take: Neither is "better" — this is about personal style and context. For a home office desk, the PCB coasters add personality. For a formal dining table, the GABNICO stone coasters disappear appropriately.

Absorbency and Practical Function

This is where the stone coasters pull ahead decisively. Diatomaceous earth is genuinely impressive as a coaster material. Set a cold beer glass on a GABNICO coaster and the condensation ring shrinks and disappears within 15 seconds, leaving the surface dry to the touch less than a minute later. For anyone who's dealt with sticky water rings on a wooden desk, this is borderline magic.

The PCB coasters cannot absorb moisture at all. They're solid circuit boards with a gold finish — if condensation forms on your glass, it'll pool on the coaster surface. You'll need to wipe it off. That said, the gold immersion surface is non-reactive and easy to wipe clean, so it's not a problem so much as a step. And if you're using mugs or glasses that don't sweat much (hot coffee, for example), absorbency is irrelevant.

Pro Tip: If you drink mostly iced beverages or live in a humid climate where everything sweats, the stone coasters are the practical choice. If you're a hot-coffee or room-temperature-drinks person, the PCB coasters work fine and look way cooler doing it.

Durability and Daily Use

Both sets are built to last, but differently. The PCB coasters are thin and rigid — at 1.6mm they won't cushion a glass from hard impact, but rubber feet prevent sliding and a generous 2-year replacement guarantee covers anything going wrong.

The GABNICO stone coasters are thicker (~6mm) and heavier, with more mass to absorb bumps and prevent sliding. The porous diatomaceous earth can absorb oils and stains over time, so regular hand washing keeps them working well — but they'll show wear faster than the non-porous PCB coasters. The included bamboo holder keeps the set organized on a shelf.

Value for Money

At $16.99 for 6 coasters ($2.83/coaster), the PCB set commands a small premium for unique material and craftsmanship. The GABNICO set is $13.99 for 6 plus a bamboo holder (~$2.00/coaster), a very competitive price for diatomaceous earth coasters.

Bottom line on value: The GABNICO coasters are slightly cheaper, but the PCB coasters offer something money can't easily replicate: uniqueness. No other coaster on your desk looks like these.

Final Verdict

🏆 Our Pick: PCB Circuit Board Coasters

We're giving the edge to the PCB coasters because a coaster's primary job isn't just to catch drips — it's to bring something to the table. Literally. These coasters turn an everyday object into a conversation starter, a desk personality piece, and a genuinely cool gift. At $16.99 for a set of 6, they're reasonably priced for what you're getting.

Yes, they don't absorb moisture like diatomaceous earth coasters. But they're also not competing on that axis — you wipe them clean and move on. For the home office, the gaming desk, or as a gift for the tech lover in your life, nothing else comes close in this price range.

If your priority is pure function — absorbency, no-wipe convenience, and minimalist aesthetics — the GABNICO stone coasters are an excellent choice. But if you want coasters that say something about you, the PCB circuit boards win hands down.

Frequently Asked Questions

Are the PCB coasters real circuit boards?

Yes — they are genuine circuit boards with real conductive traces and component footprints, not printed replicas. The immersion gold surface layer protects the traces while preserving the authentic look.

Can I put hot mugs on the PCB coasters?

Yes. The circuit boards are temperature-insensitive and handle both hot and cold drinks without issues. The rubber feet also provide a small air gap for insulation.

What's the best use case for each?

PCB coasters shine in desk or office settings where their unique look gets appreciated by visitors. The stone coasters excel in living rooms and dining tables where absorbency and no-fuss maintenance are priority.

Do the stone coasters absorb spills entirely?

They absorb condensation and small spills within 15-30 seconds. For large spills, they'll absorb what they can but won't hold an entire glass of liquid. The absorbed moisture evaporates naturally over time.
